You can try changing directories. # Uniform Resource Identifier schemes with the Remote Desktop client for Azure Virtual Desktop Feedback Summarize this article for me ## In this article 1. [Supported clients](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#supported-clients) 2. [Available URI schemes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#available-uri-schemes) 3. [Known Limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#known-limitations) 4. [Next steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#next-steps) You can use Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) schemes to invoke the Remote Desktop client with specific commands, parameters, and values for use with Azure Virtual Desktop. For example, you can subscribe to a workspace or connect to a particular desktop or RemoteApp. This article details the available commands and parameters, along with some examples. [Section titled: Supported clients](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#supported-clients) ## Supported clients The following table lists the supported clients for use with the URI schemes: Expand table | Client | Version | | --- | --- | | [Remote Desktop client for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/users/connect-windows) | 1.2.4065 and later | | [Windows App for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-app/whats-new)
_ms-avd only_ | 2.0.804.0 and later | [Section titled: Available URI schemes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#available-uri-schemes) ## Available URI schemes There are two URI schemes for supported Remote Desktop clients, _ms-avd_ and _ms-rd_. With _ms-avd_, you can specify a particular Azure Virtual Desktop resource and user with which to connect. With _ms-rd_, you can automatically subscribe to a workspace in the Remote Desktop client, rather than having to manually add the workspace. The following sections detail the commands and parameters you can use with each URI scheme. [Section titled: ms-avd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#ms-avd) ### ms-avd The _ms-avd_ Uniform Resource Identifier scheme for Azure Virtual Desktop is now generally available. Here's the list of currently supported commands for _ms-avd_ and their corresponding parameters. Important If both Remote Desktop client and Windows App version 2.0.804.0 or higher are installed on a device, the ms-avd protocol will launch a Windows App. [Section titled: ms-avd:connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#ms-avdconnect) #### ms-avd:connect `ms-avd:connect` locates a specified Azure Virtual Desktop resource and initiates the RDP session, directly connecting a specified user to that resource. **Command name:** connect **Command parameters:** Expand table | Parameter | Values | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | workspaceid | Object ID (GUID). | Specify the object ID of a valid workspace.
To get the object ID value using PowerShell, see [Retrieve the object ID of a host pool, workspace, application group, or application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/powershell-module#retrieve-the-object-id-of-a-host-pool-workspace-application-group-or-application). You can also use [Desktop Virtualization REST APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/desktopvirtualization).
_Required in Remote Desktop client_
_Not supported in Windows App_ | | resourceid | Object ID (GUID). | Specify the object ID of a published resource contained in the workspace. The value can be for a desktop or RemoteApp.
To get the object ID value using PowerShell, see [Retrieve the object ID of a host pool, workspace, application group, or application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/powershell-module#retrieve-the-object-id-of-a-host-pool-workspace-application-group-or-application). You can also use [Desktop Virtualization REST APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/desktopvirtualization).
_Required in Remote Desktop client and Windows App_ | | user | User Principal Name (UPN), for example `user@contoso.com`. | Specify a valid user with access to specified resource.
_Required in Remote Desktop client and Windows App_ | | env | **avdarm** (commercial Azure)
**usgov** (Azure Government) | Specify the Azure cloud where resources are located.
_Optional in Remote Desktop client_
_Not supported in Windows App._ | | version | **0** | Specify the version of the connect URI scheme to use.
_Required in Remote Desktop client_
_Not supported in Windows App._ | | launchpartnerid | GUID. | Specify the partner or customer-provided ID that you can use with [Azure Virtual Desktop Diagnostics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/diagnostics-log-analytics) to help with troubleshooting. We recommend using a GUID, which you can generate with the [New-Guid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/new-guid) PowerShell cmdlet.
_Optional in Remote Desktop client_
_Not supported in Windows App._ | | peeractivityid | GUID. | Specify the partner or customer-provided ID that you can use with [Azure Virtual Desktop Diagnostics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/diagnostics-log-analytics) to help with troubleshooting. We recommend using a GUID, which you can generate with the [New-Guid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/new-guid) PowerShell cmdlet.
_Optional in Remote Desktop client_
_Not supported in Windows App._ | | usemultimon | **true** or **false** | Specify whether the remote session will use one or multiple displays from the local computer.
_Optional in Remote Desktop client and Windows App_ | **Example:** Copy ``` ms-avd:connect?workspaceId=1638e073-63b2-46d8-bd84-ea02ea905467&resourceid=a0a0a0a0-bbbb-cccc-dddd-e1e1e1e1e1e1&username=user@contoso.com&version=0 ``` [Section titled: ms-rd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#ms-rd) ### ms-rd Here's the list of currently supported commands for _ms-rd_ and their corresponding parameters. Tip Using `ms-rd:` without any commands launches the Remote Desktop client. [Section titled: ms-rd:subscribe](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#ms-rdsubscribe) #### ms-rd:subscribe `ms-rd:subscribe` launches the Remote Desktop client and starts the subscription process. **Command name:** subscribe **Command parameters:** Expand table | Parameter | Values | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | url | A valid URL, such as [https://rdweb.wvd.microsoft.com](https://rdweb.wvd.microsoft.com/). | Specify a workspace URL. | **Example:** Copy ``` ms-rd:subscribe?url=https://rdweb.wvd.microsoft.com ``` [Section titled: Known Limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#known-limitations) ## Known Limitations Here are known limitations with the URI schemes: - Display properties cannot be configured via URI. You can configure display properties as an admin [on a host pool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties) or end users can configure display properties in the [Azure Virtual Desktop client](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/remote-desktop-client/overview). [Section titled: Next steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/uri-scheme#next-steps) ## Next steps Learn how to [Connect to Azure Virtual Desktop with the Remote Desktop client for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/users/connect-windows?toc=/azure/virtual-desktop/toc.json&bc=/azure/virtual-desktop/breadcrumb/toc.json).
